s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of throat discomfort with a sensation of a foreign body and odynophagia following a traumatic event
salient_findings: Persistent sensation of a foreign body in the throat
Protruding lesion through the right palatine tonsil
Uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region on radiograph
key_facts: 1-week history of symptoms
History of fish-bone impaction
Denies dysphagia, dyspnea, otalgia, or weight loss
Moderate tobacco use
Habitual betel-nut chewing
Protruding lesion is hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white in color
No visible fish bone on examination
No mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Lateral neck radiograph shows uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region

shortlist.label: Tonsillolithiasis
shortlist.why_kept: Protruding lesion is hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white in color, consistent with a tonsillolith

shortlist.label: Dystrophic calcification
shortlist.why_kept: Uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region, possibly due to previous trauma or inflammation

shortlist.label: Calcified granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hard, mobile, and well-delineated lesion with calcification, consistent with a granuloma

shortlist.label: Sialolithiasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of fish-bone impaction and symptoms of odynophagia, although less likely given the location of the calcification

shortlist.label: Foreign body reaction
shortlist.why_kept: History of fish-bone impaction and presence of a calcified lesion, although the absence of a visible fish bone makes this less likely
